scope: Internal parent lifecycle with required current-selection, ownership-record and message callbacks. No launcher/upstream activation.
behavior: Reserve exact socket intent before spawning; record child PID/birth before binding and kernel socket identity before exposing readiness. The caller retains the existing private directory.
Spend one peer-binding attempt synchronously; repeated, cancelled or lost acknowledgements never retry. Exact directory/socket identities and current-selection callbacks precede every send/message.
Snapshot outgoing objects before awaits, bound each message to 1 MiB, queued bytes to 2 MiB and in-flight operations to 64. Sequential backpressured parsing joins async consumers.
Cancellation withdraws peer readiness, closes input and joins outstanding admission, ownership and consumer callbacks. Stop verifies the direct child exit and exact socket cleanup independently.
A replaced or unacknowledged socket identity cannot be removed or reported cleaned. Rejected retirement stays rejected; no search, adoption or broad cleanup.
limits: The caller callbacks use doubles in this cohort; no production durable ownership journal or signed editor route is wired by this primitive.

The carrier and its parent do not authorize forwarding. Original upstream binding, scoped account/task protocol composition, retained Terminal launch wiring and native TUI compatibility remain unfinished.
No frontend, installed state, device, native provider task or account effects.
